whatThePageStates: The page has two sections. "Considerations" is a set of seven bold sub-headings (Resource Management, AWS Config Rules, Conformance Packs, Remediation, Aggregators, Advanced Queries) carrying eight cross-reference bullets; it states only that some AWS Config features are supported in a subset of Config Regions, and then sends the reader elsewhere for every one of those lists. It enumerates nothing itself. "List of Supported Regions" is the only enumeration on the page: a four-column table (Region Name, Region, Endpoint, Protocol) with 36 data rows, introduced as "the AWS Regions where you can enable AWS Config". Every listed Region is a positive, presence-only claim; the page never says AWS Config is unavailable in any Region and lists no No, Partial, or exclusion values. Four rows (us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2) additionally show a FIPS endpoint alongside the standard endpoint, inside the same cell.

features.featureName: AWS Config (Regions where you can enable AWS Config)
features.statuses: 36 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 36+0+0=36. The table is a presence-only allow-list: appearing in it is the Yes. There is no status column, no legend, no explicit No, and no 'isn't available' note anywhere on the page, so every non-listed Region is merely absent, not stated as unsupported. Absence must not be scored as No. Partition split of the 36: 34 in the aws (commercial) partition and 2 in aws-us-gov (us-gov-east-1, us-gov-west-1); no China (cn-*) Region appears, which is silence, not exclusion.
features.scope: None. There is exactly one dimension here: the Region. The Endpoint and Protocol columns are connection detail for the same single claim, not a second dimension of coverage. The per-feature scoping the page gestures at (rules, conformance packs, remediation, aggregators, advanced queries each supported in a subset) is delegated wholesale to six other pages and is never expressed on this page, so no per-feature scope can be read from here.
features.reasoning: The table's own lead-in names the unit of claim: Regions where you can enable AWS Config. The enumerated thing is therefore the AWS Region, which exists independently of AWS Config, making the axis external/region. One row equals one Region code equals one claim; the row count and the distinct-region count are both 36, so the rows do not collapse and distinctTargets/collapse are omitted. The unit is the whole AWS Config service, not any sub-feature: the page deliberately pushes every sub-feature's Region list to another document.

shouldNotExtract: The seven bold sub-headings in Considerations (Resource Management, AWS Config Rules, Conformance Packs, Remediation, Aggregators, Advanced Queries) and their eight bullets: these are hyperlinks to other pages, with zero enumerated values, and must not become six or seven features with an invented or borrowed count. The Region Name column (36 human-readable labels such as 'US East (Ohio)') is a second label for the same 36 Regions, not extra values. The Endpoint column: 40 hostnames across 36 rows, because four rows list both a standard and a config-fips host; hostnames are not axis values. The Protocol column, whose only value is HTTPS on every row (40 HTTPS tokens after the four doubled cells), is not a status column and 'HTTPS' is not a Yes/No. The table header row and the |---| separator row. The 'See also' Skills-for-AI-coding-assistants boilerplate and its aws agent-toolkit CLI example. The <a name=...> anchor markup.
coverageDimensions: REGION: this is the only dimension the page supplies, and it supplies it fully for the service as a whole - 36 Regions where AWS Config can be enabled, positive claims only. SERVICE: nothing. The page is about one service (AWS Config); it does not enumerate other AWS services, and it makes no statement about which services AWS Config can record. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. The page names no resource type at all; it explicitly redirects resource-type-by-Region questions to Resource Coverage by Region Availability on a different page. Any per-service or per-resource-type figure attributed to this page is fabricated. Likewise, any count for Config rules, conformance packs, remediation, aggregators, advanced queries, or the natural language query processor is fabricated here - this page links to those lists but contains none of their values.
trap:
The biggest trap is treating the Considerations section as coverage and manufacturing six or seven extra features (Resource Management, AWS Config Rules, Conformance Packs, Remediation, Aggregators, Advanced Queries, natural language query processor) from bold headings that enumerate nothing - worse still if the 36-Region count from the table below is then attached to each of them, when in fact each of those features is supported in a stated subset that this page refuses to give. Runner-up: reading the Endpoint/Protocol columns as data and inflating the count to 40, because four rows (us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2) pack a standard and a FIPS endpoint, each with its own HTTPS, into one cell via
- the extra endpoints are inside cells, not extra rows, and a FIPS hostname is not a coverage value. A third trap is inferring No for unlisted Regions (notably cn-north-1 and cn-northwest-1) and reporting a denominator of all AWS Regions with a computed No count; the page states no negatives and no total. A fourth is counting 38 by including the header and separator rows, or 37/35 by mishandling the two AWS GovCloud rows, which begin with a leading space inside the cell. A fifth is deciding the two GovCloud rows are a different axis (partition) and dropping them; they are ordinary Region rows and belong in the 36.
